scope: Bounded audit of four specified primary papers; public-source findings only. Current access/registry status was not re-audited. No website, report or publication edits.
overall_assessment: Both new metabolic-lead entries are broadly accurate. Preserve the drug/model distinctions and clarify the experimental DC interventions and study denominators.

studies.citation: Niveau C et al. Nature Communications 2025;16:1083. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-56392-x
findings: Observational sampling included blood from 87 healthy donors and 19 melanoma patients, plus 44 lymph-node/cutaneous tumour specimens; these are not a treated clinical cohort.
The intervention used BAY-8002, not AZD3965. Healthy-donor DCs were exposed to sialyl-Tn/fucose glycan mimics; seven independent experiments supported cytokine rescue (Figure 8).

Sorted DC/naive cord-blood T-cell cocultures assessed activation/metabolic orientation; representative Figure 10 endpoints used seven cocultures, cytokines six. These are not patient vaccine-response or tumour-antigen-specific efficacy results.
BAY-8002 laboratory exposure was 80 micromolar; the study establishes neither systemic clinical dosing nor human safety.
Describe glycan-induced DC functional rescue, rather than proven removal of tumour lactate or a measured CRC lactate-flux defect.
studies.row_assessment: Drug distinction is correct; improve mechanistic precision.

studies.citation: Halford S et al. A Phase I Dose-escalation Study of AZD3965, an Oral Monocarboxylate Transporter 1 Inhibitor, in Patients with Advanced Cancer. Clinical Cancer Research, 2023.
findings: Solid-tumour escalation enrolled 42 patients; 40 received a dose. Twenty enrolled patients had colorectal adenocarcinoma. Do not merge these denominators with the later expansion.

Of 39 treated patients with baseline disease assessment, nine had stable disease, 18 progression, three early progression and nine lacked follow-up response assessment. No objective responses were reported; nine were non-evaluable.

Eight dose-limiting events occurred in seven patients: five asymptomatic electroretinogram changes, two grade 3 troponin events in one patient, and one grade 3 acidosis event. Retinal-test changes were generally reversible and lacked visual symptoms.
These are AZD3965 systemic safety observations, not BAY-8002 safety or evidence of DC/vaccine augmentation.
studies.row_assessment: Current enrolled/treated/baseline distinctions and safety summary are supported.

studies.citation: Dieckmann SM et al. Journal for ImmunoTherapy of Cancer 2026;14:e014808. doi:10.1136/jitc-2026-014808
findings: Early spontaneous tg(Grm1)EPv melanoma mice received BSO plus systemic Flt3L and intratumoral poly(I:C)/anti-CD40. This expands/activates DCs; it is not an antigen-loaded DC vaccine.
Tumour-growth experiments comprised at least 12 mice/group across three experiments; tissue RNA used five/group; the exploratory survival subset had at least four/group.

The combination delayed growth, increased activated DC/T-cell infiltration and produced a survival signal. In-vitro BSO also induced ferroptotic tumour-cell death, so selective DC metabolic restoration is not established.
Three-week body/liver weight and liver-histology findings were reassuring, not comprehensive or human safety evidence.
studies.row_assessment: Broad description is correct; specify actual DC-boost regimen and avoid treating it as a clinical vaccine study.

studies.citation: Villablanca JG et al. Pediatric Blood & Cancer 2016;63:1349–1356. PMID 27092812.
findings: Recurrent/refractory neuroblastoma study: 31 enrolled, 28 dose-escalation-evaluable, 27 engraftment-evaluable and 25 response-evaluable. BSO was combined with escalating melphalan and autologous stem-cell support.
There were two partial and five mixed responses; mixed responses are not objective partial responses.

Two dose-limiting events were grade 3 transaminase elevation and streptococcal bacteremia with grade 4 hypotension/pulmonary toxicity/hypocalcemia; both resolved. These are combination-regimen observations, not BSO-alone safety estimates.

Two fatal neurological/renal toxicities discussed in the paper belonged to an earlier pilot and were attributed by those investigators to concomitant cephalosporins; do not assign them to this 2016 cohort.
studies.row_assessment: Prior human use is correctly acknowledged. Neither efficacy nor safety transfers to CRC immune augmentation.

report_conclusion: MCT1 and GCL inhibition remain low-confidence metabolic immunotherapy hypotheses. Human drug exposure and laboratory DC effects are separate evidence streams; these studies do not establish benefit or safe combination schedules with CRC vaccination, N-803, checkpoint blockade or vactosertib.
